title: Global Key Themes 2027
gist: Oxford Economics expects world GDP growth to rise from 2.7% in 2026 to 3.0% in 2027, with the outcome hinging on a durable AI boom, inflation grinding lower as oil returns to its pre-war path without a dovish central-bank pivot, and AI keeping bond yields elevated.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics estimates world GDP grew 2.7% in 2026, in line with its December forecast despite the year's volatility.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Forecasters' track record of resilience calls argues against recession-heavy positioning.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics forecasts a modest pick-up in world GDP growth to 3.0% in 2027.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Mildly pro-cyclical global backdrop for 2027 risk assets.
insights.locator: For 2027, we expect a modest pick-up

insights.claim: Oxford Economics argues the AI boom won't turn to bust in 2027 and that the recent stock-market wobble probably isn't the beginning of the end.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Treat AI-led equity drawdowns as wobbles rather than cycle tops, per this base case.
insights.quote: The recent stock market wobble probably isn’t the beginning of the end.
insights.locator: Theme 1: The AI boom won’t turn to bust

insights.claim: Whether global growth in 2027 is strong or much weaker depends chiefly on the durability of the AI boom.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: AI capex is the swing factor for global macro; monitor hyperscaler spending as a GDP leading indicator.
insights.locator: Theme 1: The AI boom won’t turn to bust

insights.claim: Oxford Economics expects the oil price to gradually decline back to its pre-war path in 2027, helping inflation grind lower.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Supports gradual downside in crude and headline-inflation breakevens through 2027.

insights.claim: Falling inflation in 2027 is unlikely to trigger a dovish pivot by central banks, per Oxford Economics.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Fade market pricing of aggressive 2027 rate cuts.

insights.claim: Oxford Economics says the AI boom was a key driver of 2026's rise in bond yields and should keep yields elevated in 2027.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: AI investment demand implies higher-for-longer term rates; be cautious on duration.
insights.quote: The AI boom has been a key driver of this year’s rise in yields
insights.locator: Theme 3: AI will dictate the path for bond yields
